tangential

/tan-JEN-shul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Tangential means only incidentally or superficially related to the main topic; off to the side of the real subject.

His tangential story about airport food had almost nothing to do with the budget question on the table.

Example

The planning committee met to decide where to build the new bike lanes. Halfway through, one member began describing a documentary he had seen about bicycle racing in the 1950s. The film touched on bikes, but it offered nothing about routes, budgets, or safety. The chair gently steered the group back, noting that the story, however entertaining, was tangential to the decision in front of them.

The story brushed against the topic of bicycles at one small point but did not bear on the actual decision, which is what tangential means.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

peripheral: Peripheral means on the outer edge of what matters - in the picture but far from its center. A peripheral issue still belongs to the discussion. Tangential is a verdict about direction: the remark touches the topic at one point and then heads off on its own line. Peripheral details sit at the margin; tangential ones lead the conversation away.

digressive: Digressive describes the wandering itself - a speaker or passage that drifts away from the main subject, often pleasantly and at length. Tangential judges the content's relation to the topic: connected at only one small point. A digressive lecturer keeps leaving the road; a tangential anecdote was barely on the road to begin with.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

central: at the heart of the matter

pertinent: directly relevant to the point

Where it sits · how far from the main topic

secondary → tangential → irrelevant

secondary vs. tangential: A secondary point still belongs to the main discussion, just with less weight, while a tangential point only brushes against the topic before heading its own way.

irrelevant vs. tangential: A tangential remark still touches the topic at one small point, but an irrelevant one has no connection to it at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — tangent: from Latin tangere, to touch; in geometry, a line that touches a circle at exactly one point

Suffix — -ial: characteristic of, pertaining to, having the nature of

Put it together: Tangential adds the suffix -ial, meaning 'characteristic of,' to tangent, the geometry term for a line that touches a circle at exactly one point, from Latin tangere, 'to touch.' A tangential comment is literally 'characteristic of a tangent': it touches the main topic at a single small point and then heads off in its own direction.

Use the root in a new word: tangible: After two years of coursework, the internship finally gave her something tangible to put in her portfolio.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal, academic/discussion register

Tangential nearly always pairs with 'to' plus the main subject (tangential to the argument, tangential to the plot). It judges how a remark or detail relates to a topic under discussion; for an unplanned side effect of an action, English reaches for a different word, collateral.
